paper_metadata.title: High-Temperature Mechanical Behavior of Cobalt-Free FeMnCrNi(Al) High-Entropy Alloys

evidence.quote: The temperature sensitivity of various microstructures of Fe45Mn15Cr15Ni25 and Fe35Mn15Cr15Ni25Al10 cobalt-free high-entropy alloys was investigated using high-temperature tensile tests.
High-Temperature Mechanical Behavior of Cobalt-Free FeMnCrNi(Al) High-Entropy Alloys

In this study, the temperature sensitivity of different components and microstructures was analyzed by examining the high-temperature mechanical behavior of Fe45Mn15Cr15Ni25 and Fe35Mn15Cr15Ni25Al10 high-entropy alloys.
The Fe45Mn15Cr15Ni25 (Al0) alloy is a single-phase recrystallized microstructure with an average grain size of approximately 30µm.
The recrystallized matrix of the Fe35Mn15Cr15Ni25Al10 (Al10) alloy contains a small amount of secondary precipitated phase, and its grain size is about 39µm.
In contrast, the A973 sample contains 24.4% of precipitated phases such as NiAl-B2 and Cr-rich phases, ranging in size from 20 nm to 4 µm.
